title: Onboarding curation: entrance kit wk0 (mentor playbook) - WIP
body:
Purpose / scope:
This is a lightweight, practical week-0 entrance kit and mentor playbook targeted at lateral IC hires and internal transfers. Goal = reduce first-week churn by giving mentors a compact script, breakpoint checklist, and interview/risk notes to validate skills post-offer. Treat as a working doc — intended to be stitched into role-specific kits (eng, product, devexp).

High-level principles (short):
- Make the first 48 hours predictable for new joiner and mentor.
- Prioritize two measurable outcomes: ability to run the dev environment and ship a tiny change; and clarity on three success signals for 30/60/90.
- Keep mentor overhead <= 2 hrs/day in week 0.
- Surface early scope mismatches quickly (within 7 days).

Quick checklist (for People Ops to hand to hiring manager / mentor before start):
- Offer accepted -> send this kit + role-specific binder 3 business days before start.
- Slack channel created + invited: #team-<name>-onboard, cc: people-ops, hiring manager, mentor.
- Access list submitted to IT: laptop, VPN, GCP project, badge request.
- First-day agenda + short bio + 30-min coffee w/ manager scheduled.
- 1st week micro-project defined (see templates below).

Mentor playbook (script with timeboxes):
Day -1 (mentor prep, 60–90 min):
- Review candidate notes + interview rubric summary (1 pager).
- Confirm micro-project and repo + CI stub are ready.
- Create simple issue: "wk0: first commit - setup and hello" and assign to new hire.
- Prepare 3 quick pairing tasks (20–30 minutes each).

Day 0 (first day, mentor time budget: 1.5–2 hrs):
- 09:00 - 09:30 intro + basics (manager + mentor): expectations, immediate priorities.
- 09:30 - 11:00 environment pairing: walk through repo, run tests, get app running locally.
- 11:00 - 11:30 micro-project kickoff: create PR skeleton, pair on README.
- Afternoon: async check-ins, invite to team standup, intro to cycle/process docs.

Day 1–3 (mentor budget: ~1 hr/day):
- 30-minute pairing session to unblock environment or PR.
- 20-minute walkthrough of observability dashboards + where to find logs.
- 10-minute heartbeat check: is role match still clear? Any surprises?

Day 4–7 (mentor budget: ~30–60 min every other day):
- Review first PR, give targeted feedback.
- Coach on how to write concise change description and tests.
- Align on 30/60/90 success signals and what autonomy looks like.

Micro-project templates (pick one, adapt per role):
- Engineering: "fix small UI bug + add unit test" (repo + issue created by mentor). Success = green CI + short PR with 1–2 small review comments.
- Infra/SRE: "add alerting for X metric + runbook stub". Success = working alert in staging + runbook doc.
- Product/PM: "decompose a small scope item into acceptance criteria and a tracking ticket". Success = clear ticket + prioritization notes.

Interview rubric one-pager (post-offer summary for mentor):
(This is a condensed scoring summary so mentors can focus on risk areas quickly)
- Technical depth (0–4): notes about system design, languages, frameworks. Red flags: inability to explain tradeoffs.
- Ownership & delivery (0–4): examples during process where candidate led a project. Red flags: no clear deliverables.
- Collaboration & communication (0–4): cross-team examples, conflict handling. Red flags: avoidance of direct feedback.
- Learning velocity (0–4): concrete examples of ramping into unfamiliar domains. Red flags: no recent learning.
- Role fit (0–4): alignment with day-to-day tasks and level. Red flags: narrow, non-transferable skillset.

Scoring guidance (quick):
- 14–20: confident hire, focus on enabling success.
- 9–13: borderline — prioritize early check-ins and a clear 30-day success contract.
- <=8: risk: escalate to hiring manager + people-ops for milestone plan.

Sample targeted probe questions for mentor to use in week 0 (short, conversational):
- "Tell me about the trickiest bug you fixed in the past 12 months. What failed first? How did you validate the fix?"
- "What’s the tightest deadline you shipped under and what tradeoffs did you accept?"
- "How do you typically write a PR description so reviewers can move fast?"
- "When did you have to learn a new tool quickly? How did you approach it?"

Rapid risk triage (if mentor perceives mismatch in first week):
- Document evidence in PR comments + quick notes in #team channel.
- 48-hour focused support: pair on one blockers session and assign a small paired task.
- 7-day check: manager + mentor + HR call to align on a 30-day remediation plan or role pivot.

30/60/90 starter template (to be filled in first week):
- 30-day: environment stable, first PR merged, two non-trivial code reviews completed, clear ownership area.
- 60-day: owns a small feature from design to deploy, identifies at least one efficiency improvement.
- 90-day: independent delivery on medium-scope tickets, proposed roadmap item or process improvement.

Doc snippets to attach in role binder (links):
- quick links to infra repos, staging credentials, observability dashboards, team runbook, code of conduct.
- suggested reading list (team-specific).

Onboarding signals dashboard (what mentors should track in week 0; one-liners):
- PR status (opened, CI green, review comments) — green if PR merged in first week.
- Dev env run time to first passing test — target < 3 hours from start.
- Response latency to team questions — target < 24 hours.

Template mentor scripts (short):
- First day: "Welcome — here's what we'll do today: get you running locally, run a test, and open a small PR. We'll block time tomorrow to finish review."
- When blocked: "Pause, take a note of the exact error, attach logs, and ping me in the channel. We'll do a short pairing session within our next sync."

Notes to people-ops (operational):
- Ship this kit in a single PDF/Doc to candidate 72h before start. Keep version and date in footer.
- Track which mentors used the kit and collect 1-line feedback after week 1.
- Iterate monthly; pick 3 metrics to measure success: time-to-first-merge, first-week sentiment (survey), and early churn (30d).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Should managers be required to create micro-projects for all roles? (pros/cons)
- How to standardize access provisioning across cloud accounts to hit <24h readiness? (follow up with infra ops)
- Add a role-specific checklist table per team — need contributions from eng/product/devexp leads.

Appendix: short boilerplate for 1-week survey (send day 8):
- Q1: How comfortable do you feel with your dev environment? (1–5)
- Q2: Did you get actionable feedback on your first PR? (yes/no)
- Q3: Did your manager/mentor set clear expectations? (1–5)
- Q4: Any blockers still unresolved? (free text)

End notes (author):
- This is intentionally terse, designed to be pasted into role-specific onboarding bundles. Use the micro-project templates as the contract for week 0.
- Please add any team-specific instrumentation snippets (CI link, staging URL) under the team binder.

-- Avery (people-ops) — WIP: please add comments inline or ping in slack thread.
